item.title: #3592207: Show notification and block user actions when maintenance mode is activated
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +503/−5 · js +475/−5 · css +28
  • Diff: 04bcf99
  • Discussion: #3592207 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

When a site goes into maintenance mode while someone has Canvas open, the editor no longer fails with an unexplained error. Canvas now shows a blurred, blocking overlay reading "Site is currently under maintenance" and stops editor actions behind it. Once the site is back online, the page redirects to the login page with a destination back to the page being edited.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

baseQuery in the Canvas UI now detects an HTTP 503 whose Content-Type does not contain json (Drupal's maintenance response is plain text or HTML, and the message is configurable, so it can be empty or valid JSON). It dispatches the new setMaintenanceMessage action, stored as maintenanceMessage in queryErrorSlice (falling back to Site under maintenance. for an empty body). A JSON 503, such as the artifact upload lock from ApiArtifactController, is still returned as a regular error. The CSRF-retry path was adjusted so a 503 on the retried request is also detected.

The request promise intentionally never settles in the maintenance case, so error boundaries, toasts and optimistic update rollbacks do not run. ErrorBoundary also renders nothing while a maintenance message is set.

The new MaintenanceModeOverlay component is rendered in App outside the error boundary. It is a Radix AlertDialog that takes focus and stops keydown propagation, so document-level shortcuts such as delete and undo cannot change the editor behind it. While shown, it sends a HEAD request to the current URL every 10 seconds. When the response is no longer 503, it navigates to getDrupalSettings().canvas.loginUrl with a destination parameter, because Drupal logs out users without the maintenance access permission. Vitest and Playwright tests cover the overlay.

  • Committed: November 14, 2026 (29 days later)

item.title: #3582851: Drupal completely breaks when installing the core block_content module alongside Canvas
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +123/−3 · php +123/−3
  • Diff: f6e4f77
  • Discussion: #3582851 · 4 contributors · 24 comments
  • Followers: 16
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 4 contributors

Summary

Enabling the core block_content module on a site with Canvas installed (reproduced on Drupal CMS) no longer breaks the site. Before the fix, the install failed partway with a missing block_content table error, and even drush cr failed afterwards, so only a database restore or reinstall recovered the site. Canvas now holds off generating block components until the module install has finished.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Core clears plugin definition caches in the middle of ModuleInstaller::doInstall(), before the new module's entity tables exist. Canvas's BlockManagerDecorator::clearCachedDefinitions() called generateComponents() for the block source right then. That triggered block discovery, and the block_content derivative queried a table that wasn't there yet. The same pattern was reported to crash Webform on sites with Trash 3.1.0.

The fix adds a public $moduleInstallInProgress flag on BlockManagerDecorator (the class loses readonly, with its constructor properties made private readonly). clearCachedDefinitions() still clears the decorated cache but returns early without generating components while the flag is set. ComponentSourceHooks::modulePreinstall() (hook_module_preinstall) sets the flag and modulesInstalled() clears it, after which Canvas generates components again. The flag lives on the service, so a container rebuild resets it. The code comments say this is safe because core rebuilds the container before hook_module_preinstall() and any later rebuild happens after the tables exist.

New kernel tests in BlockManagerDecoratorTest install block_content alone and together with contact, and check that new reusable block content still becomes a Component right after the install. The decorator carries a @todo to refactor once core issue #3001284 (cache tags for plugin derivers) lands.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 2, 2026
  • Committed: November 14, 2026 (7 months later)

Key contributors

  • phenaproxima (Acquia)
  • f0ns (Webhaven)
  • justafish (Acquia)

Collaboration

phenaproxima reproduced the failure on the latest Drupal CMS, then showed Canvas was the trigger by uninstalling it and re-enabling block_content without errors. After discussing it with mglaman, who agreed it was not a core bug, phenaproxima concluded that Canvas was populating a cache while core was clearing it. The agreed direction was to generate components lazily rather than during cache clear. The delivered fix is narrower: it skips generation only while a module install is in progress.

item.title: #3592245: Workspaces PR 13: stop deleting a named workspace when core publishes it
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +131/−135 · php +83/−43 · js +39/−79 · md +9/−13
  • Diff: b5d8f91
  • Discussion: #3592245 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

Publishing a workspace no longer deletes it. Before this change, Canvas deleted every published workspace except Main on every publish surface (Workspaces UI, Drush, cron, Canvas API), even workspaces holding no Canvas content. Now a named workspace is kept after publish, matches core's behavior, stays active for sessions that had it active, and shows no pending changes. Deleting it is left to the site admin through core's delete form, which checks delete access and refuses a workspace with children. The editor stays on the published workspace instead of reloading into Main.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Published named workspaces now persist and must be deleted manually through core's delete form; previously Canvas deleted them on publish.

Technical details

AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber::onPostPublish() now only calls clearWorkspaceStores() for the published workspace and no longer calls $workspace->delete(). This removes three problems the issue lists: the delete bypassed access checks, Workspace::preDelete() threw for a workspace with children after core had already committed the publish (the UI reported "Publication failed" while content was Live), and core's publish form hit a 404 on the deleted workspace's route. The subscriber keeps its -600 priority on WorkspacePostPublishEvent, now documented as running after core's WorkspaceTracker::onPostPublish() association cleanup (-500) so the cleared caches are not rebuilt from tracking rows core is about to remove.

With deletion gone, the fallback in CanvasWorkspacePublisher::publish() that called switchToLive() when the active workspace had vanished was removed. On the frontend, usePublishPendingChanges no longer calls window.location.reload() after publishing a named workspace; it always invalidates the Workspaces RTK Query tag to refresh the pending count. ADR 0022 and the architecture diagram were updated (post-publish now clears stores and keeps the workspace), the @todo Workspaces MR 13 comments were removed, and kernel, controller, Vitest and Playwright tests were changed to assert the workspace survives. A new kernel test, testCoreWorkspacePublishKeepsNamedWorkspace, covers a workspace with a child workspace, a second publish from the same workspace, and a workspace holding no Canvas drafts.

  • Committed: November 13, 2026 (21 days later)

item.title: #3592243: Workspaces PR 11: a failed workspace publish can leave Canvas config drafts on Live
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +258/−37 · php +229/−24 · md +29/−13
  • Diff: 977e3e8
  • Discussion: #3592243 · 1 contributor · 7 comments

Summary

On the Canvas workspaces branch, a failed publish could leave Canvas config drafts (for example code components) already saved to Live. Now a workspace that holds Canvas config drafts can be published only through Canvas. Publishing it from the core Workspaces UI, Drush or other code is refused up front with the message "This workspace has unpublished configuration changes made in Drupal Canvas. Publish it from Drupal Canvas." Nothing is written when it is refused. Workspaces without config drafts publish from every surface as before.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: Publishing a workspace that holds Canvas config drafts from the core Workspaces UI, Drush or $workspace->publish() is now refused; publish it from Canvas.

Technical details

Core's WorkspacePublisher::publish() dispatches WorkspacePrePublishEvent before it opens its own transaction. AutoSaveWorkspacePublishSubscriber::onPrePublish() saves the config fallback drafts to Live through WorkspaceAutoSave::stageFallbackDrafts() at that point, so a later failure left them Live. Only the Canvas API path, CanvasWorkspacePublisher::publish(), wraps the whole publish in a database transaction.

The change keeps that transaction on the Canvas path only. CanvasWorkspacePublisher gets a $transactionActive flag, set after startTransaction() and cleared in a finally, exposed as isActiveTransaction(). The subscriber now receives CanvasWorkspacePublisher and EntityTypeManagerInterface. If no Canvas transaction is active and hasConfigFallbackDrafts() finds a non-content entry in WorkspaceAutoSave::getAllList(), it calls $event->stopPublishing()->setPublishingStoppedReason(...) with configDraftsOutsideTransactionReason(), before anything is written. Content drafts do not count, since they are tracked revisions. Core surfaces the reason as the message of its WorkspacePublishException. The @todo Workspaces MR 11 was removed.

ADR 0022 (decisions 2 and 3, consequence 8) is updated. The limit goes away if config drafts become workspace-tracked config (work item 3592208) or if core opens its publish transaction before the pre-publish event. A rollback restores only the database: the config factory and entity caches keep what the publish wrote until reset. WorkspaceAutoSaveStagingTest gains testFailedPublishIsRolledBack() (config draft failure and revision promotion failure) and now uses the keyvalue.database factory for the fallback store so rollbacks are testable.

  • Committed: November 13, 2026 (22 days later)

item.title: #3592350: Address npm dependency security advisories
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +263/−16 · js +207/−4 · json +30/−12 · md +26
  • Diff: 6573ef1
  • Discussion: #3592350 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Canvas's JavaScript packages were updated to resolve npm audit advisories in direct and transitive dependencies. Patch releases are queued for the CLI, headless, workbench, create and ESLint config packages. Two behavior changes are worth knowing: @drupal-canvas/create now refuses to run git if certain git environment variables are set, and the ESLint config reports a missing default export at a different location with newer typescript-eslint.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Addresses npm audit advisories in Canvas's direct and transitive npm dependencies, including simple-git 3 to 4.
  • Requirements: @drupal-canvas/create now errors when GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS are set.

Technical details

simple-git in @drupal-canvas/create moves from ^3.36.0 to ^4.0.2. Per the changeset, git settings inherited from the environment (commit identity, certificates, proxies, LFS options) are still passed through, but variables that point git at another repository (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE) and GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS overrides now stop the command with an error naming the variable. A new real-git test file for useGit (use-git.js) covers this without mocks.

The root package.json overrides raise glob to ^14.0.6 and pin patched versions of minimatch (under @typescript-eslint/typescript-estree and @ts-morph/common), readdir-glob (under archiver), @joshwooding/vite-plugin-react-docgen-typescript, postcss-selector-parser and esbuild (under tsup). One package also moves zod to ^4.6.7, vitest to ^4.1.12, and the Angular example dependencies to 21.2.26.

In @drupal-canvas/eslint-config, the missing-default-export report now uses context.sourceCode.getFirstToken(node)?.loc ?? node.loc, so it lands on the first line of code with typescript-eslint 8.72 and later, as with earlier versions and the default parser.

Upgrade

If you script npm create style tooling with @drupal-canvas/create and have GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE or GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS set in the environment, unset them before running it, since the command now fails with an error naming the variable.

item.title: #3592244: Workspaces PR 12: reconcile a Live config save with the entity's drafts in every workspace
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +246/−25 · php +237/−25 · md +9
  • Diff: ade877e
  • Discussion: #3592244 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, saving a Canvas config entity (content template, pattern, code component, and so on) in Live now updates or discards that entity's draft in whichever workspace holds it. Before, only the active (staging) workspace's draft was reconciled. A template renamed or changed in Live could keep a stale draft in a named workspace, and publishing that workspace would revert the Live change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

AutoSaveManager::onCanvasConfigEntitySave() used getAutoSaveEntity(), delete() and saveEntity(), which all resolve against the staging workspace. Config has no workspace-aware storage, so a Live save never reached drafts held as fallback rows in other workspaces. It now calls the new WorkspaceAutoSave::findFallbackDraftOfEntity(), which scans AutoSaveFallbackStore::workspaceIds() and returns the workspace ID and draft of the one workspace holding a fallback row for the entity. A cross-workspace lock keeps a config draft to a single workspace. The per-draft rule is unchanged: a change to label, status, dependencies or a content template's page_variant is copied into the draft. A change to any other exported property discards it.

Discarding calls BrandKit::clearAutoSaveFileUsage(), deleteFallbackDraft() and deleteDraftBookkeeping() with the owning workspace ID. Updating re-persists the draft inside executeInWorkspaceUnchecked($workspace_id, ...), so advanceStoredBaseHash() and saveEntity() act on the owning workspace. The isPublishTimeStaging() latch is kept, so saves made during a workspace publish are not reconciled. A test shows a Live delete of a used code component discards the draft of its Component, because the Component is saved with the fallback version.

AutoSaveFallbackStore takes a new EntityLastInstalledSchemaRepositoryInterface dependency. workspaceIds() now returns [] when the workspace entity type is defined but its schema is not yet installed, since module installation can trigger Canvas config saves before the tables exist. ADR 0022 and the delete() docblock document the rule.

item.title: #3589536: Support multi-cardinality for `content-entity-reference` prop shape
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 30 files, +2105/−404 · php +1439/−378 · js +529/−16 · yml +73/−7 · md +61/−2 · mdx +3/−1
  • Diff: 1fc8e6c
  • Discussion: #3589536 · 2 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 2 contributors

Summary

Code components in Canvas can now declare a prop that holds a list of referenced entities, not just a single one. Previously a multi-value entity reference field could not be used for a content-entity-reference prop, and referenced entities past the first would be dropped. A site builder can now pick a multi-value reference field (for example "related news items") and the component receives all the referenced entities in order.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: canvas.js_component.* schema now accepts an array-of-references form for props; the MultiValuedFieldNotSupported constraint was removed.
  • New API: Code component props may be type: array with items set to the content-entity-reference shape (optional maxItems), resolving to an ordered array of entity payload objects.

Technical details

A list prop is declared as type: array with items being the content-entity-reference object shape, plus x-allowed-entity-type-id / x-allowed-bundle on items and an optional maxItems. JsonSchemaObjectRef gained isContentEntityReferenceObject() and isContentEntityReferenceObjectList(); isContentEntityReference() now matches both. JavaScriptComponent::toSdcDefinition() puts the x-allowed-* keys on items for lists, and isContentEntityReferenceObjectListProp() was added. ComponentMetadataRequirementsChecker applies the existing rules to both forms, so these props must still be optional and minItems is never allowed.

EntityFieldPropSourceMatcher::matchContentEntityReferenceShape() now takes the prop cardinality (1, or maxItems, or unlimited) and applies the same rule as scalar props, extracted to fieldCardinalityMatchesJsonSchemaCardinality(): a single reference matches only single-value fields; a list matches multi-value fields whose cardinality is at most maxItems, and an unlimited list accepts only an unlimited field. So a list is never truncated at render time. JsComponent::getExplicitInput() builds a list payload via buildReferenceListPayload() for list props and buildReferencePayload() for single ones; leaves on multi-valued fields with no delta yield arrays of values. HostEntityPropSource is never suggested for lists.

The MultiValuedFieldNotSupported constraint and validator were removed from the canvas.js_component.* config schema, and ApiUiContentEntityReferenceControllers no longer hides multi-valued fields from the picker. Docs (docs/shape-matching.md) describe the payload shapes and list three open todos (#3592326, #3592322, #3592323) around inaccessible or deleted referenced entities and empty-array output. The JS preview now omits a single reference prop from preview props when it has no value.

Upgrade

To use the new form in a code component:

featured_articles:
  type: array
  maxItems: 3
  items:
    type: object
    $ref: json-schema-definitions://canvas.module/content-entity-reference
    x-allowed-entity-type-id: node
    x-allowed-bundle: article

Existing single-reference props are unchanged.

  • Committed: November 13, 2026 (6 months later)

item.title: #3592259: Allow code components to translate interface text
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 139 files, +9652/−83 · js +6971/−58 · php +1707/−19 · mdx +361/−2 · md +266/−3 · yml +232 · json +112/−1 · css +3
  • Diff: 0c03680
  • Discussion: #3592259 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

Code components can now translate their interface text. A component calls useTranslation() from drupal-canvas/react and uses t() and formatPlural() with the same arguments as Drupal.t() and Drupal.formatPlural(). Unlike Drupal.t(), this also works when a component is exported to a headless app. When a component is published, pushed with the Canvas CLI, or imported from config, its strings appear on the User interface translation page (/admin/config/regional/translate). Translations for the page's interface language are then delivered to the component. Untranslated strings show the English source. Workbench gets a language selector for previews, and the headless SDK returns translations in page.context.translations.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: canvas.js_component.* gains an optional translatableStrings sequence of source, plural, context items, validated against Locale storage rules.
  • New API: New useTranslation() hook and TranslationsProvider in drupal-canvas/react (provider also exported by the headless-react, headless-next and headless-tanstack-start packages), optional translations key on CanvasContext, new translatableStrings property on canvas.js_component.*, and new canvas.api.interface_translation.* routes.

Technical details

Drupal does not parse JavaScript, so the tools that hold the source extract the strings: the code editor, the Canvas CLI, the Headless SDK (when building component metadata) and Workbench. All use one shared Babel scope-analysis extractor, the private @drupal-canvas/translatable-strings package. It follows bindings returned by useTranslation() (aliases, member access, shadowing) and only picks up string literals, with a context only from a static string literal in the options object. Dynamic calls are skipped silently. Invalid literals (empty string, U+0003, non-ASCII or over 255 character context) are errors: the CLI and Headless SDK builds fail, and the editor reports them.

Strings are stored in a new translatableStrings property on canvas.js_component.* config, a deduplicated sorted list of {source, plural?, context?}. An empty list means no strings and null or omitted means unknown. The schema enforces Locale's rules (NotBlank, no U+0003, ASCII context up to 255 characters). Saving a component registers its strings with Locale. Strings no component uses anymore are removed unless they are translated or have another recorded use. Metadata from older Headless SDKs that omits the property keeps the stored strings, while source saved by writers that don't send it makes them unknown (see the new ADR 23).

On Drupal-rendered pages the translations and plural formula for the page's interface language go into drupalSettings.canvasData.v0.translations, including strings of imported components. The issue describes the interface language cache context and locale cache tag on the render output. I did not verify that part in the diff. The CanvasContext translations key (type Translations: strings and optional pluralFormula) feeds the hook, and TranslationsProvider replaces rather than merges translations for components below it. t() and formatPlural() support only @ placeholders and return text, not HTML. Two new routes, canvas.api.interface_translation.languages (GET) and canvas.api.interface_translation.lookup (POST, /canvas/api/v0/interface-translation/{langcode}), served by ApiInterfaceTranslationController, let Workbench read existing translations without registering strings. They require administer code components, administer content templates or administer page template. preview-build gets a --langcode option.

Upgrade

Components that hand-edit exported config must keep translatableStrings in sync with their source. The code editor, CLI and Headless SDK derive it automatically, and the CLI's YAML validation lists it among keys authors must not provide.

  • Opened: October 27, 2026
  • Committed: November 13, 2026 (16 days later)

item.title: #3592296: Canvas AI: Show a fallback progress message when an agent calls a tool without narrating
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +448/−10 · php +448/−10
  • Diff: 55d31b1
  • Discussion: #3592296 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

In the canvas_dev_ai chat, an agent sometimes calls a tool without writing any text, so the progress message stayed unchanged and the user saw nothing happening. The progress message now gets a fallback line for each such tool call, for example "Adding Hero and Card" or "Editing Hero". Responses that include text still show only that text.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\canvas_ai\Utility\ToolProgressHelper with static helpers for building tool-call progress lines.

Technical details

CanvasDevAiBuilder::getAiProgress() now reads TextGenerated and ToolSelected status items. ToolSelected is added to the tracked types in setDetailedProgressTracking(). Items belong to one model response when they share the same time and agent runner ID. A response with non-blank text contributes only that text. A response with tool calls and no non-blank text contributes one fallback line per call, built by getToolFallbackLine().

Fallback lines by tool name: place_components gives "Adding A", "Adding A and B" or "Adding A, B and other components". edit_components gives the same with "Editing". get_component_details gives "Checking available components". Any other tool gives its configured feedback message, or Using tool: {tool name} when none is set. For place_components, the components YAML of each operation is parsed and walked in tree order (a component, then its slots, then the next component). Component IDs are deduplicated and cut to two, and labels come from the Component config entities. For edit_components, each component_uuid is resolved against the stored current layout via getComponentsByUuid(), and UUIDs not on the page are skipped. If the YAML does not parse, a component entity is missing, or no edited UUID is on the page, no line is added. This YAML and tree logic lives in the new ToolProgressHelper.

A fallback line identical to the previous fallback line is not repeated. The previous line gets a count instead, e.g. "Using tool: set_page_value (2)". A narrated response resets this. Coverage is CanvasAiDevControllerTest::testFallbackProgress().

item.title: #3592340: Show changes to the layout in the preview immediately, and keep stale server renders from undoing them
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +985/−76 · js +983/−76 · md +2
  • Diff: 3061a42
  • Discussion: #3592340 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, moving, deleting or dropping a component from the library now updates the preview straight away instead of after the server has rendered a new page. Dragged components no longer appear to jump back before landing. When several edits happen quickly, an older server render that arrives late no longer briefly removes the newer edit. A component moved by dragging is now also selected, as already happened for components added from the library.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new RTK listener middleware, optimisticPreviewListener (registered in makeStore), reacts to moveNode, shiftNode and deleteNode, so every trigger (drag and drop, context menu, "Move into", hotkeys) gets the same behaviour. It edits the DOM of the active preview iframe (getPreviewDocument()) using the canvas-start-…/canvas-end-… comment markers found via discoverCanvasBoundaries from @drupal-canvas/preview-geometry. optimisticPreview.ts provides movePreviewComponent, removePreviewComponent and insertPreviewComponent. Insertion uses the component's default_markup and css; the markup is parsed through a <template> so scripts do not run, and CSS goes in the head before the PREVIEW_HEAD_STYLES_ID style. Empty slot and region placeholders are hidden when a component lands in them, but a container that becomes empty after a move is not given a placeholder until the server render arrives. If markers are missing (for example a headless, cross-origin preview), the functions return false and the drag handler falls back to the earlier 'pending move' state.

To stop stale renders undoing these edits, previewEdits.ts keeps a module-level counter (notePreviewEdit, previewEditCount, isPreviewEditedSince). setHtml now takes the edit count at request time, stored as selectPreviewHtmlEditsAtRequest. IFrameSwapper skips applying HTML (in place or by swap) when the shown preview has been edited since that HTML was requested, and also checks this again when a loaded document is about to be swapped in. Prop edits made while typing in code component forms (createComponentFormStateHandler) also count as preview edits. Renders superseded by other changes, such as typing, still show. The server-rendered document still replaces the preview afterwards, correcting what the immediate edit approximates. useDropFromLayoutHandler now calls setSelectedComponent on the moved component.

item.title: #3592327: A code component cannot get the URL of a referenced entity, so a list of `content-entity-reference`s cannot (reliably) link to its items
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical feature request
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +97/−18 · php +83/−12 · mdx +9/−1 · yml +5/−5
  • Diff: 9980955
  • Discussion: #3592327 · 1 contributor · 6 comments

Summary

Code components that receive a content-entity-reference prop (for example a list of related news items) can now link to each referenced entity. Every entity object handed to the component carries a __url key with the entity's canonical URL, so no field pick is needed. Previously the only option was the URL alias pick, which is empty for any entity without an alias, such as taxonomy terms on a fresh site.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and front-end developers.

  • Theme change: Code components that linked via the path␞␟alias pick should switch to __url.
  • New API: Every resolved content-entity-reference payload object now includes __url, the canonical URL of the entity or null.

Summary

On the 1.x-workspaces branch, a page created in the Canvas editor while a workspace is active is now staged as published, so a single workspace publish makes it live. Before, it went live unpublished and the editor had to stage the status and publish a second time. A content template created in a workspace is now created disabled, so the core display keeps rendering for every visitor until the template's first draft is published with the workspace. item.title: #3592331: Update the preview in place on prop edits instead of reloading the iframe
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +488/−31 · js +486/−31 · md +2
  • Diff: 4364e97
  • Discussion: #3592331 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

In the Canvas editor, editing a component's props no longer reloads the whole preview iframe when only one component instance changed. That instance's markup is replaced in the live preview, or, for an island whose only change is its props, the props attribute is updated so it re-renders without going blank. This removes the flicker and the refetching of all CSS and JavaScript on each edit. Any other difference, such as changed <head> assets or drupalSettings, still loads the whole document as before.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

A new inPlaceUpdate.ts provides findInPlaceUpdate(), which compares the previous and new preview HTML by common prefix and suffix. It finds the innermost canvas-start-…/canvas-end-… comment-marker pair enclosing the whole difference and returns null if the change lies outside any instance or nothing changed. applyInPlaceUpdate() locates the marker pair in the active iframe's document, and returns false if the markers are not siblings. Otherwise it detaches Drupal behaviors from the old elements with Drupal.detachBehaviors(element, null, 'unload'), unmounts removed canvas-island elements, inserts the new markup, and calls Drupal.attachBehaviors() on the markers' parent element. When the replaced content is a single canvas-island differing only in props, the attribute is set on the live element, and only if the decoded props differ.

IFrameSwapper tracks the HTML the active iframe shows and tries an in-place update first. It falls back to the hidden-iframe load and swap when none applies. Viewport gets an inPlaceUpdates counter so unsetUpdatingComponent still fires, since an in-place update changes neither loading flag. Because it works on HTML, it covers undo and redo with no API change.

Supporting changes: the canvasDisableLinks behavior now returns early when its context has no body, since behaviors can now run with an element context. The island custom element unmounts the previous render before re-rendering when ssr is set, and unmounts nested islands replaced by a render. The attributeChangedCallback workaround that deleted Preact's private VNode property is removed.

Upgrade

Custom Drupal behaviors that run in the Canvas preview may now receive an element as context rather than the document, as canvasDisableLinks was changed to handle. Guard any use of context.body and use once() so unchanged siblings are not initialized twice.

if (!context.body) {

item.title: #3592239: Workspaces PR 8: workspace management API and switcher UI
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 49 files, +3734/−64 · js +1967/−23 · php +1349/−11 · yml +318/−26 · css +76 · md +24/−4
  • Diff: c10aa3c
  • Discussion: #3592239 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas editors can now list, create, switch to and delete workspaces from a workspace switcher in the Canvas UI. When another workspace already holds pending changes to the entity being edited, the editor shows a lock notice with the owning workspace and, if the user may view it, a way to switch. Mutating Canvas API requests are also checked against the workspace the client says it is showing, so a second browser tab that switched workspaces cannot silently write into the wrong one. The CI rule that let Cypress and Playwright failures pass on the 1.x-workspaces branch is removed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: Writing into a named (non-Main) workspace via a mutating canvas.api.* request now requires update access on that workspace.
  • New API: New hook_canvas_workspace_normalize_alter() and canvas.api.workspaces.* routes (list, create, delete, activate); optional X-Canvas-Workspace request header.

Technical details

ApiWorkspaceController (@internal) adds four routes: canvas.api.workspaces.list (GET, only top-level workspaces the user may view, plus activeWorkspaceId), create (POST with a label; the ID comes from the new WorkspaceMachineName service, validated with $workspace->validate(), 400 on failure), delete and activate. Delete uses the workspace access handler, so deleting Main is a 403; a workspace with child workspaces is a 409; deleting the active workspace first calls switchToLive(). Activation goes through WorkspaceManagerInterface::setActiveWorkspace(), so core negotiators and non-Canvas surfaces see the same workspace. WorkspaceNormalizer builds the Workspace payload (id, label, isDefault, isActive, pendingChangesCount, access.delete, access.publish) and invokes hook_canvas_workspace_normalize_alter().

WorkspaceRequestSubscriber runs on KernelEvents::REQUEST for POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE on canvas.api.* routes, except canvas.api.workspaces.*, canvas.api.log_error and canvas.api.notifications.read. If X-Canvas-Workspace is present and differs from the session's staging workspace, it throws WorkspaceConflictException::noLongerExists() or ::notActive() (409). The header is optional, so clients such as the CLI that omit it bypass the check. When staging into a named workspace, the active workspace needs update access or the request gets a 403.

The layout response from ApiLayoutController gains lockedInWorkspace (id, label, canSwitch, updated, owner), built by buildWorkspaceLockInfo() from the new WorkspaceAutoSave::getOwningWorkspaceLockInfo(). It is only built for content entities; the owner is shown only if the current user has view label access. WorkspaceAutoSave::getOwningWorkspaceId() now also covers config entities: since core's tracker does not know config drafts, it looks for a fallback-store draft in another workspace, so a config draft is locked to one workspace at a time (the editor shows no notice for config, the second editor's write gets the 409). The editor boot settings gain workspaces.activeWorkspace via buildWorkspaceSettings(). ADR 0022 and openapi.yml document the error convention: 404 for an unknown ID in the URL, 409 with source.pointer: workspace for an unusable workspace, 409 EntityLockedInAnotherWorkspace for foreign-owned entities, 403 for refused access.

Upgrade

Implement the new alter hook to add keys to the workspace payload:

function hook_canvas_workspace_normalize_alter(array &$normalized, \Drupal\workspaces\WorkspaceInterface $workspace): void {
  $normalized['myModuleReviewed'] = (bool) $workspace->get('my_module_reviewed')->value;
}

Custom API clients that know their workspace may send X-Canvas-Workspace: <workspace id> on mutating requests to get a 409 instead of a write into the wrong workspace.

item.title: #3592316: A `type: array, items: {type: object …}` prop linked to a multi-valued entity field (`EntityFieldPropSource`) gets an object of lists, not a list of objects
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Critical bug report
  • Version: 1.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +351/−15 · php +351/−15
  • Diff: acd9fe7
  • Discussion: #3592316 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

A type: array component prop with object items, linked to a multi-valued entity field in a content template, now receives a list of objects (one per field item). Before, it got a single object whose keys each held a list, so for example an image gallery with two images printed four empty <img> elements. No update path is needed, since only the expression is stored, not its evaluated value. Single-cardinality fields and expressions with an explicit delta evaluate as before.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: withDelta(int $delta): static added to EntityFieldBasedPropExpressionInterface and implemented by FieldPropExpression, FieldObjectPropsExpression and ReferenceFieldPropExpression.

Technical details

Evaluator::doEvaluate() evaluated each key of a FieldObjectPropsExpression over the whole field item list. Validation did not catch it, because core's ComponentMetadata added object to the type of every prop (per the issue; core 11.5 no longer does, see #3591948). StaticPropSource with FieldTypeObjectPropsExpression already evaluated once per field item.

Now, when the expression is a FieldObjectPropsExpression, the field cardinality is not 1 and getDelta() is NULL, doEvaluate() loops over the field items and re-evaluates $expr->withDelta($delta) for each. The results are merged into one EvaluationResult so cacheability and attachments of every object are kept, including objects that are then dropped. Empty objects (for instance when every object prop needs a referenced entity that was deleted) are filtered out and the list is reindexed with array_values(), so the type: array prop gets no gaps.

withDelta() is a new method on EntityFieldBasedPropExpressionInterface. FieldPropExpression sets the delta, FieldObjectPropsExpression sets it on itself and on every object prop expression, and ReferenceFieldPropExpression sets it only on the referencer, since the referenced expression targets another entity's field. Tests added: a multi-valued daterange case in EntityFieldPropSourceTest, rendering image-gallery with an unlimited image field in NodeTemplatesTest, broken-reference cases, and PropExpressionTest::testWithDelta().

Upgrade

Any custom class implementing EntityFieldBasedPropExpressionInterface must now implement public function withDelta(int $delta): static.

Summary

item.description:

Summary

In the 1.x-workspaces branch, the Canvas publish review panel now publishes the whole workspace at once. The per-change checkboxes, "Select all" and "Publish N selected" are gone, replaced by a single "Publish now" button and an "N unpublished changes" count. The side-by-side review button becomes "Review all changes", which walks every reviewable change. A conflicted change blocks publishing until it is resolved. Refusals that concern the workspace as a whole, such as core refusing to publish an item in an unpublished moderation state, now show in the error list under "Workspace".

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: Publishing now goes through core workspaces, so the e2e/test setups grant view any workspace, edit any workspace and create workspace alongside publish auto-saves.
  • New API: drupalSettings.canvas.workspaces.stagingWorkspaceId is now exposed to the UI, and a canvas_e2e_support.update_live test route (LiveEntityController::updateLive) saves the Live copy outside any workspace.

Technical details

ui/src/services/pendingChangesApi.ts: publishAllPendingChanges takes no argument. It POSTs to /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/publish with { workspace, pendingChanges }. workspace comes from getStagingWorkspaceId(), which reads drupalSettings.canvas.workspaces.stagingWorkspaceId. The server now sets that value from workspaceAutoSave->getStagingWorkspaceId(), so a tab whose workspace was switched elsewhere cannot publish a different workspace. pendingChanges maps each auto-save key to its data_hash from the cached getAllPendingChanges result. Before building the body it waits for in-flight preview and layout auto-save mutations and refetches the list, so a publish right after an edit isn't refused as "edited after the review". On a 409 it restores the previous pending changes and sets the conflicts and errors. On success it clears the whole pending cache.

PublishReview loses its selection state, and onPublishClick is called without arguments. UnpublishedChanges passes all unpublished changes to the hook's cleanup. onReviewSelectedChanges is replaced by onReviewAllChanges, and conflicted pages and non-page changes are excluded from the walk. The review is still gated on isReviewUxEnabled(). A refused publish drops the snapshot, so discarding the refused changes afterwards doesn't flash "Published". ReviewErrors labels errors whose source.pointer is workspace as "Workspace". Errors tied to no entity (code 11 for a discarded key, validation violations, server errors, plain 403 strings) are counted in the header but not listed. Auto-save keys are now workspace-scoped (e.g. canvas_default:canvas_page:1:en). PageStatus therefore finds the homepage staged config update with findInChanges instead of an exact key lookup.

The Playwright specs were rewritten for this. canvas_e2e_support gets a LiveEntityController route that simulates external edits to Live, and a new article_moderation recipe fixture backs a spec checking that a draft moderation state refuses to publish. Two @todo Workspaces MR 8 and MR 9 markers remain for the workspace switcher, lock notice and Draft badge.

Tests or custom code that drove per-item publish must change. Replace the selection clicks (canvas-publish-review-select-all, Select change <title>, Publish N selected) with a click on the Publish now button. Test roles that publish need core workspace access, as in the updated setups:

'publish auto-saves',
'view any workspace',
'edit any workspace',
'create workspace',

item.title: #3592237: Workspaces PR 7a: the workspace is the unit of publish (back end)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +1616/−1489 · php +1578/−1471 · yml +38/−18
  • Diff: 45a7694
  • Discussion: #3592237 · 1 contributor · 2 comments

Summary

In the 1.x-workspaces branch, the Canvas publish endpoint now publishes the whole active workspace as one unit, through core's workspace publish, instead of publishing selected auto-save items one by one. The request must name the workspace and list the pending changes the editor reviewed. If the workspace is not the active one, or the pending list has changed since the review, the request is refused with a 409 and nothing is published. Any invalid item blocks the whole publish with a 422. Discarding a draft is now refused when the user cannot update the entity, or when another workspace has locked it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: Publishing now also requires core's publish access to the active workspace, not only the Canvas publish permission. The publishChanges UI flag in drupalSettings follows the same rule. Discarding an auto-save now requires entity update access.
  • API change: POST /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/publish now publishes the whole active workspace. The body must be {workspace, pendingChanges}, where pendingChanges maps auto-save key to data_hash. A body without them is a 400. Per-item selection and the old 409/424 codes for unexpected/unmatched items and global assets are gone. DELETE /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/{entityTypeId}/{entityId} gains 403 and 409 responses.
  • New API: New \Drupal\canvas\Workspace\CanvasWorkspacePublisher service (marked @internal), new ErrorCodesEnum cases ActiveWorkspaceMismatch (10) and PendingChangesOutdated (11), and a BuildsAvatarUrlTrait.

Technical details

ApiAutoSaveController::post() is rewritten and the per-item machinery is removed: sibling-translation expansion, global asset dependency checks, applyAutoSaveTranslationSnapshots(), conflict-aware validation, the manual transaction, and AutoSaveManager::groupContentEntityAutoSaves(). post() returns a 400 if workspace or pendingChanges is missing. It throws WorkspaceConflictException::noLongerExists() or ::notActive() (codes 9 and 10) when the named workspace is gone or is not the active one. It checks core's publish access on the workspace and returns a 403 if denied. stalePendingChangesResponse() then compares the reviewed key => data_hash map with getPublishableAutoSaves(). It returns a 409 with one PendingChangesOutdated (code 11) error per added, edited or discarded key.

The actual publish goes through the new CanvasWorkspacePublisher::publish(). It wraps core's $workspace->publish() in a database transaction, covering the pre-publish subscribers that apply staged config as well as core's own revision promotion. It runs inside executeInWorkspace() and counts the auto-save rows for the success message. If the publish fails, it restores the previously active workspace, because core only switches back after the callback returns. If the published workspace was deleted and is still active in the session, it switches to Live. In the controller, WorkspacePublishValidationException maps to a 422 with one error per item, and any other WorkspacePublishException from core or a subscriber maps to a 409 with pointer workspace and no code. Other exceptions become a 500. An empty workspace returns 204 'No items to publish.'

ApiAutoSaveController::get() now adds the workspace cache context. delete() calls WorkspaceAutoSave::assertNotLockedInAnotherWorkspace() (409, with the owner in meta.workspace per openapi.yml) and checks entity update access after the 404 check. CanvasController computes publishChanges from the Canvas permission combined with core's publish access to the staging workspace, and adds that access result's cacheability to the response. buildAvatarUrl() moved into BuildsAvatarUrlTrait. ContentTemplate::autoSavePublish() is kept, because WorkspaceAutoSave::stageFallbackDrafts() still calls it. openapi.yml documents the new PublishAllRequest schema and the extra responses. Two @todo Workspaces MR 22 markers note that non-default-translation rows are still hidden from the pending list and the published count.

Upgrade

Clients of the publish endpoint must stop sending per-item selections. The body is now:

{
  "workspace": "spring_campaign",
  "pendingChanges": { "<auto-save key>": "<data_hash>" }
}

pendingChanges is the map returned by GET /canvas/api/v0/auto-saves/pending. Callers that relied on the old 409/424 item codes (UnexpectedItemInPublishRequest, UnmatchedItemInPublishRequest, GlobalAssetNotPublished) should handle the new codes 10 and 11 and the code-less 409 from a pre-publish gate. Users publishing need core's publish access to the workspace, which the tests grant through the edit any workspace permission.

item.title: #3592256: Add `dr canvas:audit:usage` command
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Canvas
  • Type: Major feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 14 files, +926/−175 · php +817/−171 · md +57/−4 · json +52
  • Diff: 23b82c3
  • Discussion: #3592256 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Canvas now has a dr canvas:audit:usage command that lists where components are used. Give it a component source plugin ID (for example sdc), a component ID, or a component ID and version separated by @. It reports usages in content entity revisions, config entities (such as patterns) and auto-saves. This helps when you need to find where a known-broken component or version has been placed. Use --revisions=all|default|latest to narrow which content revisions are searched, and --format=table|json for human or machine output. The component audit page also now lists config entity usages only under the component version their tree actually uses. Before, it listed them without regard to version.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: ConfigAuditBase::getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget() and componentTreeUsesAuditTarget() accept $version_ids, getAutoSavesUsingAuditTarget() no longer throws for versions, and getComponentTreeConfigEntityTypeIds() is now public.
  • New API: New dr canvas:audit:usage command (requires Drupal >= 11.4 dr CLI) with a versioned --format=json report described by docs/audit-usage.schema.json.

Technical details

AuditUsageCommand (marked @internal) is a thin wrapper over the existing ComponentAudit service that powers the component audit page. It resolves the target to pairs of component and versions: a component source plugin ID expands to all components of that source, a bare component ID to all of its versions, and ID@version to one version. Unknown targets, unknown --format or --revisions values, and a missing target with --no-interaction exit with 2. When the target is omitted in interactive mode, it prompts for source, then component, then version.

The JSON report is an envelope with report_version (AuditUsageCommand::REPORT_VERSION, 1), target, revisions and usages. Each usage has component, version, kind (content, config or auto-save), entity_type, id, revision, default, latest and label. revision, default and latest are null for config and auto-save usages. Auto-save labels come from the auto-saved entity. The command first searches all requested versions at once, and only repeats the search per version when that finds something.

The audit layer needed version support to make this work. Config entity dependencies come from the config dependency graph, which does not track versions. So getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget() now takes $version_ids and inspects each dependent's component tree when versions are given. ComponentAudit::componentTreeUsesAuditTarget() checks getComponentVersion() on each item. ColorAudit throws a LogicException if versions are passed, since colors have no versions. The "not yet implemented" exception in getAutoSavesUsingAuditTarget() is removed. ComponentAuditController::createConfigTable() now passes [$component->getLoadedVersion()]. The diff also adds docs/cli.md, a contributor doc listing rules that every Canvas dr command must follow, and kernel tests.

Upgrade

Callers that previously relied on getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget($component, $type) ignoring versions are unaffected, because $version_ids defaults to []. To restrict to specific versions, pass them, for example getConfigEntityDependenciesUsingAuditTarget($component, $config_entity_type_id, [$version]). Subclasses of ConfigAuditBase must update their componentTreeUsesAuditTarget() signature to (ComponentTreeItemList $tree, ConfigEntityInterface $target, array $version_ids = []): bool.

  • Opened: October 27, 2026
